scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8090: HELP!! One whole group of machines has been ERASED from
the network!! From my PC, every other group works EXCEPT that one -- they are
gone for me, though the people over there swear their machines are fine among
themselves. Something around the routers' route list must be wrong, but I
don't know what. Could someone look at it so I can reach them again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. OSPF converged across the core, so every
  internal prefix -- including 172.16.30.0/24 -- is present as a dynamic route and
  reachable. PC1 (10.5.0.1) reaches a 172.16.30.x host (e.g. 172.16.30.254) with
  0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single missing OSPF prefix that is in fact installed.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- 10.5.0.0/24 unable to
reach 172.16.30.0/24 because the OSPF route is missing -- is NOT reproducible:
OSPF has converged, 172.16.30.0/24 appears as an OSPF route in the core
(`show ip route ospf` lists it), and PC1 (10.5.0.1) reaches 172.16.30.254 with
0% loss, just like every other Campus 1 prefix.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the route for 172.16.30.0/24 is
present and forwarding, and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed path (10.5.0.x -> 172.16.30.x), finds it working,
inspects the OSPF route table for 172.16.30.0/24, sees it installed, and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a missing prefix or blames the core OSPF process
to match the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: A complete four-phase diagnostic sweep of the Kath4 topology found no current fault. Phase A (L2/infrastructure): all 28 devices scanned with zero ACL drop rules, zero duplicate MAC addresses, and all 15 host machines confirmed to have both an IPv4 address and a working default route. Phase B (control plane): all nine FRR/OSPF daemons are active with healthy vtysh sockets; every router holds full OSPF adjacencies and carries exactly 17 OSPF routes — matching the 17 unique network prefixes in the topology. The routing tables of the four critical gateway devices (mswitch0, sshswitch, router16, router17) were inspected directly; each table contained all required prefixes pointing to correct next-hops with no static overrides or blackhole entries. Phase B targeted pings confirmed the three cross-group paths that the initial reachability scan had not covered: pc5 (VLAN10) → pc1 (VLAN5), pc5 (VLAN10) → pc12 (VLAN30), and pc1 (VLAN5) → pc12 (VLAN30) all returned 0% loss. Phase D (resource pressure): zero suspect devices. No routing fault, link fault, ACL block, MAC conflict, or resource contention is present in the live network state. The user's report of one "erased" group is unconfirmed by any observable evidence: there is no missing prefix, no wrong next-hop, no flap script, and no daemon or syslog trace of a past disruption. Root cause: no anomaly exists in the current network state. Fix: no corrective action is required; advise the user to re-test and verify whether their host's local ARP cache or application state has been cleared.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes 172.16.30.0/24 is present as an OSPF route and reachable from 10.5.0.0/24 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms all OSPF prefixes are present (no missing prefix) and explicitly shows pc1 (VLAN5 -> 10.5.0.0/24) to pc12 (VLAN30 -> 172.16.30.0/24) ping returned 0% loss.

The agent's investigation log shows the commands run and their outputs (reachability map, infra/L2 sweep, OSPF snapshot, routing table checks, and targeted pings) that directly support the writeup's claims. The conclusions logically follow from the observed healthy adjacencies, presence of the OSPF route in RIBs, and successful cross-VLAN pings, so the negative-control diagnosis is well justified.
